newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London shrug off Iraq, Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London shrug off Iraq, Wall St.

text.p: Japanese stocks were steady in late afternoon dealings in London on Tuesday, taking heart from the higher close in Tokyo and shrugging off a weak opening on Wall Street and the U.S. attack on Iraq.
The Nikkei 50 index in London was up 0.30 point at 1,377.50 in late dealings after the Nikkei in Tokyo gained 0.45 percent, closing above the crucial 20,000 point level.
"The Iraqi situation is not too bad as yet and currency factors look favourable at the moment," a London dealer said.

Traders said reports suggesting the Japanese government might postpone a supplementary budget could help the market as it could result in a helpful delay to a feared rise in consumption tax. But prices were largely expected to hold steady on Wednesday, traders said, noting that the Dow Jones index was paring early losses.
A rise in oil prices worldwide was expected to boost demand for Japanese oil stocks but interest so far had been limited.
"We've had a few enquiries about Nippon Oil but not too many are willing to dip their toes," the dealer said.
